title: A finite completely decomposed etale family descends to a finite stage
statement: Let $(R_\alpha)_\alpha$ be a directed system of commutative Noetherian rings with Noetherian direct limit $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and set $S_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}R_\alpha$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Fix $\alpha_0$, a finite type $S_{\alpha_0}$-scheme $P_{\alpha_0}$, and finitely many morphisms $v_{j,\alpha_0}:V_{j,\alpha_0}\to P_{\alpha_0}$, with every $V_{j,\alpha_0}$ of finite type over $S_{\alpha_0}$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $P_\alpha,V_{j,\alpha},v_{j,\alpha}$ and $P,V_j,v_j$ for their base changes [def-pc-fibre-product] to $S_\alpha$ and $S$. Assume that each $v_j$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and that the family is completely decomposed: for every $p\in P$ there are $j$ and $z\in V_j$ above $p$ such that the canonical residue field map $\kappa(p)\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]. Then there is $\alpha_1\geq\alpha_0$ such that for every $\alpha\geq\alpha_1$, every $v_{j,\alpha}$ is etale and the family $(v_{j,\alpha})_j$ is completely decomposed. The assertion includes empty schemes and an empty family when its target is empty.

source.place: Expose III Lemma 3.1.1 and its proof by a finite closed filtration with sections on successive differences, printed p.38; the same argument applies to a finite family by taking its disjoint union. The rings and models here are Noetherian as in that lemma.

proof.text: First verify the finiteness hypotheses on the given models. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $P_{\alpha_0}$ and $V_{j,\alpha_0}$ are Noetherian, hence quasi-compact; [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes them quasi-separated. Each $v_{j,\alpha_0}$ is locally of finite type: near a source point choose finite-type affine charts over an affine base chart and shrink the source to a principal affine lying over a target affine chart. If its coordinate ring is generated over the base ring by $b_1,\ldots,b_m$, the same generators generate it over the target coordinate ring, whose image contains that base ring. The target chart ring is Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] therefore makes this ring map finitely presented. Thus $v_{j,\alpha_0}$ is locally of finite presentation. The same reasoning applies to any morphism between finite-type models over $S_\alpha$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], such morphisms are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so these $v_{j,\alpha_0}$ are of finite presentation. All these finiteness properties persist under base change by that node.

source.place: Expose III Lemma 3.1.1 and its proof by a finite closed filtration with sections on successive differences, printed p.38; the same argument applies to a finite family by taking its disjoint union. The rings and models here are Noetherian as in that lemma.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $S=\varprojlim S_\alpha$: the affine limit is the spectrum of the ring colimit. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit], $P=\varprojlim_{\alpha\geq\alpha_0}P_\alpha$, with affine transition maps. All $P_\alpha$ are qcqs by Step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale] to each given $v_{j,\alpha_0}$, using its local finite presentation from Step 1. Finiteness of the family gives a common stage where all are etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] they remain etale at every later stage.

source.place: Expose III Lemma 3.1.1 and its proof by a finite closed filtration with sections on successive differences, printed p.38; the same argument applies to a finite family by taking its disjoint union. The rings and models here are Noetherian as in that lemma.

proof.text: Form $V=\coprod_j V_j$ and $v:V\to P$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The open components cover $V$, so $v$ is locally of finite presentation, as each $v_j$ is. The pointwise hypothesis says exactly that $v$ is completely decomposed. The target $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], hence qcqs by Step 1. Apply [lem-per-cd-finite-presentation-section-cover] to obtain finitely many finitely presented immersions $i_a:Z_a\to P$ covering $P$ and lifts to $V$. Replace $Z_a$ by the finitely many inverse images of the open-and-closed components $V_j$. Each is open and closed in $Z_a$, is Noetherian, and is quasi-compact; its inclusion is locally of finite presentation (the local rings are unchanged). By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] it is of finite presentation. Composition preserves local finite presentation by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition], and their quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness give finite presentation over $P$ by the same permanence node. Restricting a closed immersion to an open-and-closed source piece is again closed: on affine charts it is the quotient followed by the idempotent quotient selecting that piece. Thus the restricted maps are still immersions. These finitely many pieces still cover $P$, and their immersions and lifts now have the form $i_a:Z_a\to P$, $s_a:Z_a\to V_{j(a)}$, with $v_{j(a)}s_a=i_a$. Empty pieces can be omitted.

source.place: Expose III Lemma 3.1.1 and its proof by a finite closed filtration with sections on successive differences, printed p.38; the same argument applies to a finite family by taking its disjoint union. The rings and models here are Noetherian as in that lemma.

proof.text: Factor each immersion as $Z_a\xrightarrow{c_a}O_a\xrightarrow{o_a}P$, with $c_a$ closed and $o_a$ open, by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Choose $O_a$ quasi-compact: the image of the quasi-compact $Z_a$ is covered by finitely many affine opens contained in the original open factor; their union can replace that factor, and the restricted closed immersion still has source $Z_a$. The scheme $O_a$ is locally Noetherian, as an open subscheme of $P$, and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. The open immersion is locally of finite presentation, since on affine charts it is a localization at one element. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] it is of finite presentation. The $Z_a$ are already finitely presented over $P$ by Step 3, and now so are the $O_a$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-family-descent] to the system $(P_\alpha)$ to model them simultaneously at one stage. This does not yet assert that the model arrows are immersions.

source.place: Expose III Lemma 3.1.1 and its proof by a finite closed filtration with sections on successive differences, printed p.38; the same argument applies to a finite family by taking its disjoint union. The rings and models here are Noetherian as in that lemma.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-diagram-lift-of-models] over the base system $(P_\alpha)$ for the objects $P$, $V_j$, $Z_a$, $O_a$, retaining the prescribed models of $P$ and $V_j$. Lift $c_a,o_a,s_a$ and impose the finitely many equations $v_{j(a)}s_a=o_ac_a$. Its hypotheses hold: the $V_j$ have finitely presented models over $P_{\alpha_0}$ by Step 1, and the other models were obtained in Step 4. The output equations are exact at a common finite stage, and remain exact on every later base change. Write $i_{a,\alpha}=o_{a,\alpha}c_{a,\alpha}$. Since all model objects are finite type over the Noetherian $S_\alpha$, the maps $c_{a,\alpha},o_{a,\alpha},i_{a,\alpha}$ are locally of finite presentation by the affine argument of Step 1.

source.place: Expose III Lemma 3.1.1 and its proof by a finite closed filtration with sections on successive differences, printed p.38; the same argument applies to a finite family by taking its disjoint union. The rings and models here are Noetherian as in that lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion] to the finitely many $c_{a,\alpha}$ and [lem-weil-pbc-descend-open-immersion-qcqs] to the $o_{a,\alpha}$. Their source and target models are qcqs, their limit maps are the specified closed and open immersions, and their required local finite type/presentation hypotheses were checked in Step 5. At a common stage the $i_{a,\alpha}$ are immersions. Closed immersions persist by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; open immersions persist by the stated all-later-stages clause of the cited descent node. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-finite-family-joint-surjectivity-stage], applied to the finite family $i_{a,\alpha}$, makes it jointly surjective at every later stage. Here the target is $P_\alpha$ itself, the sources are finitely presented over it, the arrows are locally of finite presentation, and their limit images cover $P$ by Step 3. Choose $\alpha_1$ above this stage and the etale stage of Step 2.

source.place: Expose III Lemma 3.1.1 and its proof by a finite closed filtration with sections on successive differences, printed p.38; the same argument applies to a finite family by taking its disjoint union. The rings and models here are Noetherian as in that lemma.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha\geq\alpha_1$ and $p\in P_\alpha$. Step 6 supplies $t\in Z_{a,\alpha}$ with $i_{a,\alpha}(t)=p$; put $z=s_{a,\alpha}(t)\in V_{j(a),\alpha}$. Step 5 gives $v_{j(a),\alpha}(z)=p$. The immersion $i_{a,\alpha}$ induces an isomorphism $\kappa(p)\to\kappa(t)$: for its closed factor use [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso], and its open factor identifies local rings by [def-weil-open-immersion]. By [def-weil-residue-field], this isomorphism factors as $\kappa(p)\xrightarrow{u}\kappa(z)\xrightarrow{w}\kappa(t)$. Identify $\kappa(t)$ with $\kappa(p)$ through the composite. Then $wu=1$; since the unital field map $w$ is injective, $wuw=w$ implies $uw=1$. Thus $u$ is an isomorphism. This is the required complete decomposition at every later stage, while Step 2 supplies etaleness. If the family is empty, the hypothesis forces $P=\varnothing$; the section cover can be empty and Step 6, whose finite-family lemma allows an empty family, forces $P_\alpha=\varnothing$ eventually. Hence the asserted empty cases are included.
